meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Secondary conversational sense ('there is, there are') (present есть; у меня есть = I have) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: там такие деньги = there's so much money in it

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: + genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice
Secondary conversational sense ('there isn't') (+ genitive) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'of course'.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'roll, roulade' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Иначе все поймут, что за рулём пьяный!
examples.trans: Otherwise everyone will realise the driver is drunk!

meanings.note: + genitive: 'из мэрии' = from the town hall

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, я уже знаю. Мне звонили из мэрии.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I already know. The town hall called me.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'veal' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Одна телятина, треска и свежий салат!
examples.trans: One veal, cod, and fresh salad!

examples.text: Мясные рулетики из телятины с тонкими ломтиками ветчины.
examples.trans: You know, veal rolls with thin slices of ham.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'ham', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Это нежное мясо с тонкой ветчиной.
examples.trans: This is tender meat with thin ham.

examples.text: Мясные рулетики из телятины с тонкими ломтиками ветчины.
examples.trans: You know, veal rolls with thin slices of ham.

examples.text: Это такая штука для нарезки ветчины очень тонкими ломтиками.
examples.trans: It is a gadget for slicing ham really thin.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
goes right before the word it negates
понимаешь? = you know? do you understand?

examples.trans: I want to go to the sea, you know?

examples.text: Я хочу нормально жить! Я хочу биде, понимаешь?
examples.trans: I want to live like a normal person! I want a bidet, do you understand?

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'красть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to steal', paired with 'красть'.

examples.text: Чтобы он вернул деньги, которые украл.
examples.trans: For him to give back the money he stole.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('my') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
culinary instructions or doctor's prescription

examples.trans: Before you is a unique ancient recipe.

examples.text: Шеф хранит этот секретный рецепт в тайне.
examples.trans: The chef keeps this secret recipe confidential.

examples.text: Шеф хранит свой тайный рецепт супа.
examples.trans: The chef keeps his secret soup recipe.

meanings.note: usually in the genitive ничего, with не: ничего не осталось

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to take', forming an aspectual pair with 'взять'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
'брать' alone often means this, in talk about officials

examples.trans: We have to take all the money.

meanings.note: hesitation, at the start of a sentence
Secondary conversational sense ('oh come on!') (ну, папа!) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'corpse, dead body' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Well, Senya, you are a corpse.

examples.text: Детство у меня было трудное. Я вырос в коммуналке.
examples.trans: My childhood was hard. I grew up in a communal flat.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: in the instrumental: 'кем ты работаешь?'

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'then'.
Secondary conversational sense ('then, in that case') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'can', forming an aspectual pair with 'смочь'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to believe', forming an aspectual pair with 'поверить'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to believe in') (верить в + accusative) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Go on, tell her. Nina doesn't believe it.

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'honest' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.

examples.text: Я ухожу. Ваш сын будет бедным и честным.
examples.trans: I'm leaving. Your son will be poor and honest.

meanings.note: 'дать слово' = to give one's word, 'держать слово' = to keep one's word
'дать слово' = to give one's word, 'держать слово' = to keep one's word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: the 'е' drops out in the other forms
Secondary conversational sense ('' ' = over and out') (radio and phone phrase) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: At the end of the film everyone is happy.
